QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_40

question.text: Which of the following correctly describes the relevant non-institutional client-level position limit for cash-settled IRD on G-Sec?

answer.text: 3% of open interest or INR 400 crore (8-11 year bucket) / INR 200 crore (4-8 and 11-15 year buckets), whichever is higher
Lower of 3% of outstanding stock of underlying bond or Rs. 500 crore
Lower of 5% of open interest or Rs. 500 crore
3% of outstanding stock with no absolute floor

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook ties the relevant non-institutional client limit to open interest, with an absolute floor that varies by maturity bucket: 3% of open interest or INR 400 crore for the 8-11 year bucket, and 3% or INR 200 crore for the 4-8 and 11-15 year buckets - whichever is higher. The Trap: The rule is open-interest based, not outstanding-stock based; the absolute amount acts as a floor (higher-of), not a cap (lower-of). INR 500 crore is not a source-backed client figure. The 5% percentage is also incorrect. Note: Pages 234-235 set out the client-level limits, and page 237 reinforces that positions are monitored based on total open interest and specified in lots.
